셋.forms: native · counting things, hours, age · before a counter: 세 (세 개, 세 시)
셋.x: There are three of us in my family.
셋.t: Before a counter 셋 becomes 세: 세 명, 세 시.

닫다.x: Be sure to close the door when you leave.
닫다.e: Opposite of 열다 (open). Don't mix it up with 닦다 (wipe) — similar spelling.
닫다.t: Regular verb — not ㄷ irregular like 듣다. 닫다 → 닫아요.

싫다.e: 싫어요! = 'No, I don't want to.' 싫어하다 = to dislike.
싫다.t: 싫다 takes 이/가 (비가 싫어요); 싫어하다 takes 을/를 (비를 싫어해요). Pronounced [실타]; 싫어요 [시러요].

길이 막히다.forms: 길이 막혀요 · 길이 막혔어요 · 길이 막힐 거예요
길이 막히다.m: there's a traffic jam, the roads are congested
길이 막히다.x: I was late for the meeting because of traffic this morning.
길이 막히다.t: "길이 막혀서 늦었어요" is the classic Korean excuse for being late.

마당.ex: 할머니 댁 마당에서 강아지가 놀고 있어요.
마당.x: A puppy is playing in the yard at Grandma's house.
마당.t: 마당 is an open yard of dirt or pavement; a yard planted with flowers and trees is a 정원.

음력.x: My grandmother celebrates her birthday by the lunar calendar.
음력.t: Pronounced [음녁] — nasalization; the solar calendar is 양력.

사업.x: My father runs a small restaurant business.
사업.t: 사업을 하다 means 'to run your own business,' not just to work at a company.

감상.ex: 제 취미는 음악 감상과 영화 감상이에요.
감상.x: My hobbies are listening to music and watching movies.
감상.e: Literally 'examine and admire.' Homonym 감상 means one's impressions or thoughts.
감상.t: 음악 감상 and 영화 감상 are the standard ways to list hobbies on forms or in self-introductions.

활용하다.m: to make use of, to utilize, to apply
활용하다.x: I use my spare time to study Korean.
활용하다.e: Literally 'living use' — putting something to active use.
활용하다.t: Unlike plain 사용하다, 활용하다 suggests using something cleverly or to its full advantage.

무역.x: Korea's economy developed greatly through trade.

염색하다.x: I dyed my hair brown at the hair salon.
염색하다.t: The usual pattern is 머리를 [color]으로 염색하다.

구입.x: You can purchase tickets at the ticket office.

제정.m: enactment, establishment (of a law or rule)
제정.ex: 정부는 새로운 법의 제정을 추진하고 있습니다.
제정.x: The government is pushing for the enactment of a new law.

개정.ex: 법이 개정되어서 다음 달부터 규칙이 바뀝니다.
개정.x: The law was revised, so the rules change starting next month.

주민등록증.m: resident registration card, national ID card
주민등록증.ex: 은행에서 계좌를 만들 때 주민등록증이 필요해요.
주민등록증.x: You need your national ID card to open a bank account.
주민등록증.t: Pronounced [주민등녹쯩]; in conversation people often shorten it to 주민증.

덜렁대다.forms: 덜렁대요 · 덜렁댔어요 · 덜렁댈 거예요 · 덜렁대지 마세요
덜렁대다.m: to be careless, to be scatterbrained
덜렁대다.x: I'm scatterbrained, so I often lose things.
덜렁대다.e: Mimetic 덜렁 'loosely, carelessly' + -대다 'keep doing'; a scatterbrain is 덜렁이.
덜렁대다.t: Describes a habit more than a single act; 덜렁거리다 means the same.

저항하다.ex: 많은 시민들이 부당한 권력에 끝까지 저항했습니다.
저항하다.x: Many citizens resisted unjust power to the end.

받아들이다.m: to accept, take in; to adopt (an idea)
받아들이다.x: He gladly accepted his friend's advice.

호평.x: This album received favorable reviews from critics.

겨냥하다.x: This product was made with women in their twenties in mind.
겨냥하다.e: From the noun 겨냥 'aim'; close in sound and meaning to 겨누다 'to point (a weapon)'.

언중유골.m: words with a hidden barb, a pointed remark
언중유골.x: My friend said it with a smile, but there was a sting in the words.
언중유골.e: Literally 'there's a bone inside the words'.
언중유골.t: Native equivalent: 뼈 있는 말 'words with a bone in them'.

취약점.ex: 회사 보안 시스템에서 심각한 취약점이 발견되었습니다.
취약점.x: A serious vulnerability was found in the company's security system.

기독교.ex: 한국에는 기독교를 믿는 사람이 꽤 많아요.
기독교.x: There are quite a lot of people in Korea who believe in Christianity.
기독교.e: 기독 is a sound transliteration of 'Christ', via Chinese; the syllables carry no real meaning.
기독교.t: In everyday Korean, 기독교 usually means Protestant Christianity; Catholicism is called 천주교.

잠복기.x: The incubation period of this virus is usually about five days.

췌장.ex: 췌장은 혈당을 조절하는 인슐린을 만드는 기관이에요.
췌장.x: The pancreas is the organ that makes insulin, which controls blood sugar.
췌장.e: Literally 'pancreas organ'; -장 = internal organ: 심장, 신장, 간장.

담낭.x: I had surgery because gallstones formed in my gallbladder.
담낭.t: In everyday speech the native word 쓸개 is more common.

안면인식.ex: 공항에서 안면인식으로 출국 심사를 받을 수 있습니다.
안면인식.x: At the airport, you can go through departure screening with facial recognition.
안면인식.t: 안면 is a formal word for 얼굴; 안면이 있다 means 'to be acquainted'.

지식재산.x: Creators' intellectual property should be protected by law.
지식재산.t: The older term 지적재산 means the same thing; 지식재산 is now the official term.

서정.ex: 그의 시에는 고향에 대한 따뜻한 서정이 담겨 있어요.
서정.x: His poems hold a warm lyrical feeling for his hometown.
서정.e: Literally 'pouring out feeling'; contrasts with 서사 'narrative'.
서정.t: Most often used as 서정적: 서정적인 음악, 서정적인 분위기 'lyrical music, a lyrical mood'.

대작.ex: 이 영화는 제작비만 300억 원이 든 대작이에요.
대작.x: This movie is a blockbuster that cost 30 billion won just to make.
대작.e: Literally 'big work' — large in scale or ambition.
대작.t: -작 means 'a work' and builds many words: 대작, 역작, 수작, 졸작, 유작, 습작.

오비이락.m: a suspicious coincidence, unlucky timing that invites blame
오비이락.ex: 오비이락이라고, 내가 들어가자마자 컴퓨터가 고장 났어요.
오비이락.x: Talk about bad timing — the computer broke the moment I walked in.
오비이락.e: Literally 'the crow flies off, the pear falls' — so the crow gets blamed.
오비이락.t: The native proverb version is 까마귀 날자 배 떨어진다.

신경전달물질.ex: 도파민과 세로토닌은 우리 뇌의 대표적인 신경전달물질입니다.
신경전달물질.x: Dopamine and serotonin are typical neurotransmitters in our brain.
신경전달물질.t: Pronounced [신경전달물찔]: ㅈ after ㄹ becomes tense.
